questions.question: Around 1911, Delray Beach experienced a major farming and canning boom centered around tomatoes and which tropical fruit?
questions.explanation: Pineapple and tomato farming boomed in early Delray around 1911, inspiring the name of downtown's historic Pineapple Grove Arts District.

questions.question: Built originally as schoolhouses in 1913 and 1925 at Atlantic and Swinton Avenues, what is the name of Delray Beach's historic cultural campus?
questions.explanation: Old School Square preserved Delray's 1913 elementary school (Cornell Art Museum) and 1925 high school (Crest Theatre) as a downtown cultural anchor.

questions.question: On which U.S. federal holiday is the CrossFit Hero WOD 'Murph' traditionally performed across gyms nationwide?
questions.explanation: Gyms across the country perform 'Murph' every Memorial Day to honor fallen Navy SEAL Lt. Michael P. Murphy and all service members who made the ultimate sacrifice.

questions.question: Which U.S. military branch uses the official motto 'Semper Fidelis' (Always Faithful)?
questions.explanation: 'Semper Fidelis' was officially adopted as the motto of the United States Marine Corps in 1883.

questions.question: What is the highest U.S. military decoration awarded for personal valor in combat above and beyond the call of duty?
questions.explanation: Established in 1861 for the Navy and 1862 for the Army, the Medal of Honor is the nation's highest award for military valor in action.

questions.question: Before settlers renamed the town Delray in 1901, what was the settlement originally named after its founder from Michigan?
questions.explanation: Former Michigan Congressman William S. Linton bought 160 acres in 1894 and platted the town as Linton before settlers renamed it Delray in 1901.

questions.question: Established in 1942 just south of Delray Beach, which WWII installation served as a major Army Air Forces radar training base?
questions.explanation: Boca Raton Army Air Field trained thousands of airmen in wartime radar technology; portions of the former base later became Florida Atlantic University.

questions.question: Before becoming a CrossFit Hero WOD, what nickname did Navy SEAL Lt. Michael Murphy give his 1-mile run, 100 pull-ups, 200 push-ups, 300 squats, 1-mile run workout?
questions.explanation: Lt. Murphy called the workout 'Body Armor' because he routinely performed it wearing a 20-lb weighted vest or body armor.

questions.question: Founded on June 14, 1775, by the Continental Congress, which is the oldest branch of the United States Armed Forces?
questions.explanation: The Continental Army was established on June 14, 1775—four months before the Navy (Oct 1775) and five months before the Marine Corps (Nov 1775).

questions.question: During World War II, why were coastal towns like Delray Beach ordered to enforce strict nighttime blackouts?
choices: To reserve electrical grid capacity for local radar towers
To stop German U-boats from spotting Allied ships silhouetted against shore lights
To avoid distracting night-training bombers from Boca Raton
To reduce radio frequency interference along the coastline
questions.explanation: Bright shoreline lights silhouetted Allied tankers offshore, making them easy targets for German U-boats operating along Florida's Atlantic coast.

questions.question: In what year was the mainland town of Delray officially incorporated (prior to its 1927 merger with barrier-island Delray Beach)?
questions.explanation: The mainland town of Delray incorporated in 1911; the barrier island incorporated separately in 1923, and the two merged into the City of Delray Beach in 1927.

questions.question: Which top-secret WWII Army Signal Corps radar school between Jupiter and Stuart is preserved today as Jonathan Dickinson State Park?
questions.explanation: Opened in 1942 across more than 11,000 acres, Camp Murphy housed the Southern Signal Corps School before closing in November 1944.

questions.question: Founded around 1904 near modern Delray Beach and Boca Raton, which Japanese-American farming settlement inspired the Morikami Museum after WWII land condemnation?
questions.explanation: Led by Jo Sakai, the Yamato Colony lost much of its farmland to the Boca Raton Army Air Field in 1942. Colonist George Morikami later donated land for the museum.

questions.question: Delray Beach's Spady Cultural Heritage Museum occupies the 1926 home of local educator Solomon D. Spady, who studied under which famed scientist?
questions.explanation: Solomon D. Spady studied under George Washington Carver before arriving in Delray Beach in 1922 and leading the Delray County Training School until 1957.

questions.question: The barbell Hero WOD 'DT' (5 rounds of 12 deadlifts, 9 hang power cleans, 6 push jerks) honors Staff Sgt. Timothy P. Davis, who served in which U.S. branch?
questions.explanation: U.S. Air Force Staff Sgt. Timothy P. Davis was killed in action in Afghanistan on February 20, 2009, while supporting combat operations.

questions.question: In U.S. CrossFit gyms, what is the standard weight of a full-size men's barbell?
questions.explanation: A standard U.S. men's barbell weighs 45 lbs (while IWF metric men's bars weigh 20 kg, or ~44.1 lbs).

questions.question: What are the three standard heights (in inches) on a classic CrossFit 3-in-1 wooden plyometric box?
questions.explanation: Standard 3-in-1 plyo boxes measure 20" x 24" x 30", matching standard women's Rx (20") and men's Rx (24") box jump heights.

questions.question: What are the standard CrossFit Rx wall-ball target heights for men and women?
questions.explanation: CrossFit Rx standards set the wall-ball target at 10 feet for men (20-lb ball) and 9 feet for women (14-lb ball).

questions.question: Which muscle group on the front of the thigh is the primary knee extensor when driving up from a heavy front squat?
questions.explanation: The four muscles of the quadriceps straighten the knee joint and take center stage in upright front squats, thrusters, and wall balls.

questions.question: The four muscles of the rotator cuff primarily stabilize which joint?
questions.explanation: The rotator cuff keeps the head of the humerus centered in the shoulder socket during overhead lifts, kipping pull-ups, and presses.

questions.question: In International Weightlifting Federation (IWF) color coding, what color is a 20 kg bumper plate?
questions.explanation: IWF competition bumper colors: Red = 25 kg, Blue = 20 kg, Yellow = 15 kg, and Green = 10 kg.

questions.question: A traditional 1-pood Russian kettlebell weighs 16 kg—closest to which standard pound weight used in CrossFit?
questions.explanation: A 16 kg kettlebell equals ~35.3 lbs. Standard CrossFit pairings are 16 kg (35 lb), 24 kg / 1.5 pood (53 lb), and 32 kg / 2 pood (70 lb).

questions.question: On a Concept2 RowErg, moving the damper lever from 1 to 10 directly adjusts what?
choices: Mechanical brake pressure against the chain
How much air enters the flywheel housing (drag factor)
The calorie multiplier used by the PM5 monitor
Bungee recoil tension inside the monorail
questions.explanation: The damper opens or closes the vent on the flywheel housing, altering airflow and drag factor rather than adding fixed brake resistance.

questions.question: During the controlled lowering phase into the bottom of a back squat, what type of contraction are your quadriceps performing?
questions.explanation: An eccentric contraction occurs when a muscle lengthens under tension—such as controlling your descent into a squat or lowering a pull-up.

questions.question: Which large diamond-shaped muscle of the upper back elevates and retracts the shoulder blades during cleans, snatches, and farmer's carries?
questions.explanation: Upper, middle, and lower trapezius fibers shrug, retract, and stabilize the scapulae under heavy overhead and pulling loads.

questions.question: Which anatomical plane divides the body into left and right halves—the primary plane of motion for squats, deadlifts, and running?
questions.explanation: Forward-and-backward flexion and extension movements like squats, lunges, and running occur in the sagittal plane.

questions.question: Compared to a men's 28 mm Olympic barbell shaft, what is the IWF-standard shaft diameter of a women's 15 kg Olympic barbell?
questions.explanation: IWF specifications set women's 15 kg Olympic bars at a 25 mm shaft diameter, making hook-grip wrapping easier for smaller hands.

questions.question: What is the standard IWF sleeve diameter (where bumper plates load) shared by both men's and women's Olympic barbells?
questions.explanation: Both men's (20 kg) and women's (15 kg) Olympic barbells use 50 mm (~2 inch) sleeves so standard bumper plates fit interchangeably.

questions.question: What is the name of the bracing technique where a lifter takes a deep abdominal breath and pushes against a closed airway to create intra-abdominal pressure during a max lift?
questions.explanation: The Valsalva maneuver increases intra-abdominal and intra-thoracic pressure, turning the torso into a rigid cylinder that protects the spine under heavy loads.

questions.question: Which of the following muscles is NOT one of the four rotator cuff ('SITS') muscles?
questions.explanation: The four rotator cuff muscles (SITS) are Supraspinatus, Infraspinatus, Teres minor, and Subscapularis. Serratus anterior protracts the scapula.

questions.question: Which Eminem song from the '8 Mile' soundtrack opens with 'Look, if you had one shot, or one opportunity...'?
questions.explanation: Released in 2002, 'Lose Yourself' won the Academy Award for Best Original Song and remains one of the most-played PR tracks in gym history.

questions.question: Which Metallica classic from 'The Black Album' (1991) features the chorus 'Exit light, enter night'?
questions.explanation: 'Enter Sandman' has one of rock's most recognizable build-ups for heavy barbell attempts and walkouts.

questions.question: Which 1982 Survivor rock classic was commissioned by Sylvester Stallone for 'Rocky III'?
questions.explanation: 'Eye of the Tiger' spent six weeks at #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and became the quintessential training montage anthem.

questions.question: Which 1990 AC/DC opener from 'The Razors Edge' inspired a famous CrossFit burpee/squat WOD tied to every time the crowd chants the title?
choices: You Shook Me All Night Long
questions.explanation: Angus Young actually alternate-picked the rapid studio intro riff for 'Thunderstruck' (while famously miming hammer-ons in the video).

questions.question: Which 2003 White Stripes anthem is powered by one of the most recognizable stadium chant riffs in sports and gym warm-ups?
choices: Fell in Love with a Girl
questions.explanation: Off the 2003 album 'Elephant,' Jack White played the signature bass-like riff on a semi-acoustic guitar run through a pitch-shift pedal.

questions.question: Which 1992 Rage Against the Machine anthem builds through the refrain 'And now you do what they told ya'?
questions.explanation: Off their self-titled 1992 debut album, 'Killing in the Name' is a box staple for heavy conditioning finishes.

questions.question: Which 1980 AC/DC track from 'Back in Black' features 13 ominous tolls of a massive bronze bell in its intro?
questions.explanation: Opening 'Back in Black,' 'Hells Bells' uses 13 tolls of a custom-cast bronze bell—an unmistakable countdown before a WOD clock starts.

questions.question: Which 1997 Foo Fighters classic opens with 'Hello, I've waited here for you' and drives at a brisk 158 BPM?
questions.explanation: Featured on 'The Colour and the Shape,' 'Everlong' is a box favorite for fast rowing, running, and double-under intervals.

questions.question: Which 2005 Fort Minor track breaks down grit into 'ten percent luck, twenty percent skill, fifteen percent concentrated power of will'?
questions.explanation: Released by Linkin Park co-founder Mike Shinoda's side project Fort Minor, 'Remember the Name' remains a staple on competition floors.

questions.question: Which 2005 Dropkick Murphys Celtic-punk anthem featured in 'The Departed' adapted unpublished lyrics written by folk icon Woody Guthrie?
questions.explanation: Featured on 'The Warrior's Code' (2005) and Martin Scorsese's 'The Departed' (2006), 'I'm Shipping Up to Boston' brings instant sled-push adrenaline.

questions.question: Linkin Park and Jay-Z collaborated on the 2004 mashup EP 'Collision Course,' winning a Grammy for which workout staple?
questions.explanation: 'Numb/Encore' won the 2006 Grammy Award for Best Rap/Sung Collaboration and still dominates gym playlists.

questions.question: Which 2002 Eminem track featuring Nate Dogg on 'The Eminem Show' was never released as a commercial single yet became one of Spotify's top workout songs?
questions.explanation: Despite never being issued as a radio or retail single, ''Till I Collapse' became the first non-single to surpass 1 billion Spotify streams.

questions.question: Kanye West's 2010 heavy-lift anthem 'POWER' famously samples '21st Century Schizoid Man' by which progressive rock band?
questions.explanation: 'POWER' (from 'My Beautiful Dark Twisted Fantasy') samples a live version of King Crimson's 1969 prog-rock classic '21st Century Schizoid Man.'

questions.question: DMX's classic CrossFit anthem 'Party Up (Up in Here)' originally appeared on which multi-platinum 1999 album?
choices: It's Dark and Hell Is Hot
Flesh of My Flesh, Blood of My Blood
questions.explanation: Released on '...And Then There Was X' in December 1999 (and as a single in February 2000), 'Party Up' became DMX's biggest crossover hit.

questions.question: Kendrick Lamar's 2017 #1 hit 'HUMBLE.' won how many Grammy Awards at the 60th Annual Grammy Awards?
questions.explanation: 'HUMBLE.' won 3 Grammys (Best Rap Performance, Best Rap Song, and Best Music Video), while its parent album 'DAMN.' also won Best Rap Album.

questions.question: How many calories (kcal) are provided by 1 gram of protein and 1 gram of carbohydrate?
questions.explanation: Both protein and carbohydrates provide 4 kcal per gram, while alcohol provides 7 kcal/g and fat provides 9 kcal/g.

questions.question: How many calories (kcal) are in 1 gram of dietary fat?
questions.explanation: Fat is the most energy-dense macronutrient at 9 kcal per gram—more than double protein or carbohydrates.

questions.question: What is the stored form of carbohydrate kept in your muscles and liver to power high-intensity CrossFit workouts?
questions.explanation: Muscle glycogen is your rapid-access fuel tank for intense glycolytic efforts like 8-to-15-minute metcons.

questions.question: Which primary electrolyte is lost in the largest concentration through sweat during humid Delray Beach training sessions?
questions.explanation: Sweat is primarily water and sodium; heavy sweaters can lose over 1,000 mg of sodium per hour in South Florida heat.

questions.question: Which fat-soluble vitamin is produced in the skin from sunlight and supports bone density and immune health?
questions.explanation: Vitamin D aids calcium absorption and supports bone strength, muscle function, and immune health.

questions.question: Which electrolyte works alongside sodium to regulate fluid balance and nerve impulses, and is rich in potatoes, avocados, and bananas?
questions.explanation: Potassium works via the sodium-potassium pump to support muscle contractions, nerve signaling, and cellular hydration.

questions.question: Which trace mineral sits at the center of hemoglobin to carry oxygen in your blood to working muscles?
questions.explanation: Iron is essential to hemoglobin and myoglobin; low iron stores can cause fatigue and reduce aerobic conditioning output.

questions.question: Which macromineral acts as a cofactor in over 300 enzymatic reactions—supporting ATP production and muscle relaxation—and is rich in spinach, almonds, and dark chocolate?
questions.explanation: Magnesium supports energy metabolism, neuromuscular relaxation, and sleep recovery.

questions.question: Found naturally in red meat and fish, which compound is widely supplemented at 3–5 g daily to regenerate ATP during heavy, explosive lifts?
questions.explanation: Creatine boosts intramuscular phosphocreatine stores, supporting repeat power output in heavy sets and short sprints.

questions.question: EPA and DHA—abundant in salmon, sardines, and mackerel—belong to which class of essential fatty acids?
questions.explanation: Omega-3 fatty acids support cardiovascular health, cell membrane fluidity, and balanced recovery inflammation.

questions.question: Which essential branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) acts as the primary biochemical trigger for muscle protein synthesis via the mTOR pathway?
questions.explanation: All three BCAAs (leucine, isoleucine, valine) support muscle metabolism, but leucine is the primary signal that activates mTOR protein synthesis.

questions.question: Which water-soluble vitamin is a required enzymatic cofactor for synthesizing collagen to repair tendons and ligaments?
questions.explanation: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is essential for hydroxylation steps during collagen cross-linking in tendons, ligaments, and skin.

questions.question: Chronic supplementation with beta-alanine raises muscle concentrations of which intracellular buffer that counters hydrogen ions during intense 1–10 minute metcons?
questions.explanation: Beta-alanine is the rate-limiting precursor to carnosine, which buffers intracellular H+ ions and helps delay fatigue during anaerobic efforts.

questions.question: Roughly how long can stored intramuscular ATP and phosphocreatine (PCr) alone sustain maximal-effort explosive output (such as a 1RM lift or all-out sprint)?
questions.explanation: The ATP-PCr system supplies immediate maximal power for roughly 0–10 seconds before rapid glycolysis takes over.

questions.question: Unlike most water-soluble vitamins that clear quickly in urine, which vitamin is stored in substantial liver reserves that can last for years?
questions.explanation: The human liver stores large reserves of Vitamin B12 that can last two to several years, unlike most other water-soluble vitamins.
